instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Confess Around Them
cards.instruction: Use partial admissions to make a reciprocal confession feel like the only missing piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll work out why nobody reached the meeting. I moved it to three. What happened to the room?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You moved it without telling me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Put that under my name. I'll send the correction once you've told me where you sent everyone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: First tell me why you didn't warn me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I thought you'd veto three. I'll put that in the message too. Which room do I need to apologise for?

cards.title: It Was Foreshadowed
cards.instruction: Turn the failure into a planned turning point by returning to earlier details that now appear to predict it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring the bowls. That wobble was the start of the trifle, right on cue.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said it was a wedding cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It was, until the layers settled. I'll make the custard; you can explain the change to the guests.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not telling them you meant it to collapse.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just bring the bowls, then. I'll tell them why I let it wobble.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Coats on. I said that loose peg would matter; this is the outdoor part of our weekend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were supposed to fix it before the tent fell.

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: Be Right in Retrospect
cards.instruction: Perform certainty by reinterpreting every surprise as something your earlier words were obviously predicting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get the water out. When I said the evening would flow, I was clearly onto something.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You meant the conversation, not a burst pipe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And what are we all talking about? Bring me a bucket; I'll manage the kitchen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Forget the bucket. Turn the water off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Point me to the valve and I'll do it. You have to admit I was right about the flow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll sort the refund. I said this holiday would have a sunny ending, and a cheque will brighten things up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said sunny weather. We spent a week indoors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which is why we're getting the money back. Give me the receipts; I'll make the call.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You booked it. You explain why we packed sunglasses for a flood.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll tell them I chose the dates. When the cheque comes, I want you to remember who forecast a sunny ending.

cards.title: Reverse the Score
cards.instruction: Turn each apparent loss into a new category of victory, then invite comparison on those changing terms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Follow me back to the car. Last in the race, first to spot the kingfisher.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was first to finish. It was a race.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You keep the medal. How many birds did you notice on the way?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was watching the finish line.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I win for range, then. You set the pace back; I'll point out everything you missed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll arrange the trophies. Mine fits on the top shelf; yours needs its own table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is the consolation prize. Mine says first.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You choose the spot. I'll put mine beside it; let's see who can go longest without mentioning a trophy.

cards.title: Return to the First Hope
cards.instruction: Return to an early hope after every setback, expanding its meaning until the whole scene seems to fulfill it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll make this cottage ours. We wanted a place we knew every inch of.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole roof needs replacing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll know every tile. I'll get the quotes; you can choose who does it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Even the cheapest might take all our savings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll read the figures together before we sign. If we spend the savings, I want us sitting under a roof we chose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll start the village singalong. We said this concert would bring everyone together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The power's out. Nobody can hear you at the back.

beats.speaker: A

beats.text: Then hold the first song. You meet them at the door; I'll make room up front for our new lighting crew.
